title: San Diego FC: Historic Playoff Berth & MLS Cup Contender - World Today News
content: San Diego FC made history by clinching a playoff berth in its debut MLS season, highlighted by a 2-1 win over the San Jose Earthquakes that propelled the club to the top of the Western Conference standings. The club’s success is underscored by a 4-3 loss to Houston Dynamo in a road thriller, illustrating the competitive nature of the league. The article outlines the MLS Cup playoff structure, noting that the tournament begins on October 22 with Wild Card matches and includes a best‑of‑three series in Round One. Key dates and formats are provided, positioning San Diego FC as a potential MLS Cup contender for the 2025 season. The narrative remains factual, citing match results and playoff details without editorializing.

title: MLS playoff clinching scenarios: San Diego FC can be first to secure berth
content: According to the USA Today article, San Diego FC, the expansion club, currently sits atop the Supporters' Shield (tied with FC Cincinnati) and Western Conference standings, and could become the first team to clinch a playoff berth on MLS Decision Day 2025 (Oct. 18). The article lists a series of scenarios in which San Diego would secure a spot, such as a win or draw for San Diego combined with losses or draws for FC Dallas, Austin FC, Colorado Rapids, Real Salt Lake, or San Jose Earthquakes. It also notes that D.C. United and CF Montréal are the only teams that could be eliminated from playoff contention this weekend. The 2025 MLS Cup Playoffs will feature 18 teams, with the top nine from each conference qualifying; the eighth- and ninth-place finishers play wild‑card matches, and the top seven seeds enter a best‑of‑three Round 1. The playoff schedule runs from Oct. 22 (wild‑cards) to Dec. 6 (MLS Cup). According to BetMGM, Inter Miami CF is the current favorite to win the championship, followed by San Diego FC, Vancouver Whitecaps, FC Cincinnati, Los Angeles FC, Minnesota United, and Philadelphia Union.

title: San Diego FC clasifica a la postemporada de la MLS Cup
content: San Diego FC secured a berth in the MLS Cup playoffs after a 0‑0 draw with Portland at Snapdragon Stadium. The club, whose offensive attack ranks fourth in the league, controlled about 60 % of possession but failed to convert that advantage into goals. The result keeps San Diego at the top of the Western Conference with 54 points, and they have lost only two of their last eleven matches (excluding Leagues Cup fixtures). Fans were forced to silence their cheers when two goals were disallowed – one for Hirving 'Chucky' Lozano and another for Anders Dreyer – both ruled off‑side. Meanwhile, the San Diego Padres defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers at Petco Park to claim the National League West title. San Diego will face LAFC on Saturday, August 30, while Portland will travel to Minnesota.

title: Playoff-bound San Diego FC has hopes for more in an already strong first season
content: San Diego FC, the league's newest expansion club, became the fastest expansion team to reach the MLS playoffs, clinching a berth in 28 games—shorter than the 2009 Seattle Sounders' 29‑game run. The team secured the spot with a 0‑0 draw at home against the Portland Timbers on Saturday, April 5, 2025. With 53 points, San Diego sits one point behind the Eastern Conference leaders, Philadelphia Union, and is in a tight race for the Supporters' Shield, a title no expansion team has ever won. The club is also on pace to set a new expansion points record, surpassing LAFC's 57 points in 2018. Midfielder Anders Dreyer, who has 13 goals and a league‑leading 17 assists, said, 'Of course, qualifying for the playoffs, it's amazing and it's a nice accomplishment for the team. And to do it so early, it's also nice, but we're still aiming with six games left to keep getting a lot of points.' Forward Jeppe Tverskov added, 'I think our feeling is right now that we are in the playoffs. So now the first step is complete and we are in a position where I feel like we can hold our chest high and say we want to go for it all.' Coach Mikey Varas emphasized the club's vision: 'When there's clear vision, as players or staff or as a club, you have a target to reach for, and then you hire the right people, and you sign the right players, people who are overachievers. Now they have that target, and then you get enough people who want to go beyond that target, then you have the potential for something special to happen.' San Diego is owned by Egyptian billionaire Mohamed Mansour and the Sycuan Tribe, the first Native American tribe to hold an ownership stake in a professional soccer team. The club's Right to Dream Academy, founded in Ghana in 1999, operates on Sycuan tribal land in El Cajon, California.

title: First-place San Diego FC out to derail Quakes' playoff hopes
content: San Diego FC, sitting atop the Western Conference with a 17‑8‑6 record and 57 points, has clinched a playoff berth and is targeting the Supporters' Shield. With three matches remaining, the club will host the San Jose Earthquakes, who are 11th in the West with 35 points and are fighting for the final postseason spot. San Diego's coach Mikey Varas said, 'I think we're fortunate to come out with a point,' after a 1‑1 draw at Atlanta that ended 1‑0 to Anders Dreyer at halftime before a penalty tied the game. San Diego tied the 2018 LAFC for most points by an expansion team; a win would break St. Louis City's 17‑game record. San Jose, whose defense has allowed 58 goals in 31 fixtures, has been criticized by coach Bruce Arena, who said, 'The same problem we've had all year,' following a 3‑1 loss to St. Louis. The upcoming match could keep San Diego at the top and potentially eliminate San Jose from playoff contention.

title: MLS Cup Playoffs: Who's In, Prospective Playoff Matches and Qualification Scenarios
content: The 2025 MLS Cup Playoffs are approaching, with all Eastern Conference playoff spots already secured, though final seeding remains undecided. The Philadelphia Union have clinched the top seed and will face the winner of the Wild Card match in the first round. FC Cincinnati has locked in a top-four spot and aims for the second seed in their match against CF Montréal on Decision Day. Inter Miami remains in contention for a top-two finish with two games left. In the Western Conference, two playoff spots remain open, with FC Dallas, Real Salt Lake, Colorado Rapids, and San Jose Earthquakes still in contention. FC Dallas, with 41 points and two games remaining, are the frontrunners and could secure a playoff berth with a single win, potentially finishing with 47 points. Real Salt Lake, with two games left against Seattle and St. Louis CITY SC, could reach a maximum of 46 points; they may clinch with a win over Seattle, especially without key midfielder Diego Luna. The Colorado Rapids, despite summer additions like Paxten Aaronson, must beat LAFC on Decision Day to have a chance; a draw would suffice only if Real Salt Lake loses both remaining games, while a win is needed to surpass FC Dallas even if Dallas drops both games. San Jose Earthquakes, after a 4-1 loss to Vancouver, are not yet mathematically eliminated; they could qualify via a win over Austin FC on Oct. 18 if at least one of Colorado, Salt Lake, or Dallas loses both remaining matches. The final day of the regular season, Oct. 18, is critical for determining the final playoff matchups and seeding.

title: Comparing San Diego FC's Historic Debut Season to Other MLS Expansion Teams
content: San Diego FC made history in their inaugural MLS season by becoming the most successful expansion team in regular season history, reaching 60 points after a 4-2 victory over the Houston Dynamo in their penultimate game. The team finished with 18 wins in 33 games, surpassing LAFC’s previous record of 57 points set in 2018. Anders Dreyer led the club with 18 goals and 17 assists, while Hirving 'Chucky' Lozano recorded 9 goals and 10 assists in 32 games. With their record secured, San Diego FC is poised to clinch the top seed in the Western Conference and could become only the second expansion team ever to win the MLS Cup in their debut season. Comparisons are drawn to other expansion campaigns: LAFC (2018) earned 57 points with a 16-9-9 record, featuring Carlos Vela and Diego Rossi; St. Louis CITY SC (2023) achieved 56 points and topped the Western Conference with a 17-12-5 record, led by João Klauss and Nicholas Gioacchini; the Chicago Fire (1998) set a record of 20-2-12 with 56 points and won both MLS Cup and the U.S. Open Cup; and Atlanta United (2017) earned 56 points with strong performances from Josef Martínez (19 goals), Miguel Almirón, and Héctor Villalba, though they were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs. Despite varied outcomes, San Diego FC’s 60-point season stands as the highest in MLS expansion history.

title: History! San Diego FC set two MLS expansion records | MLSSoccer.com
content: San Diego FC, in their inaugural Major League Soccer (MLS) regular season, achieved a historic milestone by earning 60 points with a record of 18 wins, 9 losses, and 6 draws, as of October 5, 2025. With one match remaining, they lead the Western Conference table and are aiming to secure the No. 1 seed in the Audi 2025 MLS Cup Playoffs. Head coach Mikey Varas praised the team's achievement, stating, 'You have to celebrate that man. You have to celebrate that – 60 points,' adding that 'nobody can take that away from us. That's written down right now until somebody else breaks it.' The team's success is attributed to top-tier talent, including Chucky Lozano, who contributed 9 goals and 10 assists and returned to the Mexican national team, and Anders Dreyer, who recorded 35 goal contributions (17 goals, 18 assists) and is in contention for both MLS Newcomer of the Year and the Landon Donovan MVP Award. USMNT player Luca de la Torre and other key contributors also played vital roles in the team's record-setting performance.

title: Expansion side San Diego first to clinch postseason spot after 0-0 draw with Timbers
content: San Diego FC, an expansion club, secured its first postseason berth by holding Portland Timbers to a 0‑0 draw on Saturday night. Goalkeeper CJ dos Santos recorded his ninth clean sheet of the season with two saves, one in each half, while the match left San Diego with a 16‑7‑5 record. Timbers goalkeeper James Pantemis made one save in his fourth shutout in 13 starts, finishing with a 10‑9‑8 record. San Diego has achieved six consecutive road wins, the most for a first‑year club, and is four points shy of Los Angeles FC’s 57‑point record from 2018. The Western Conference leaders need one more win to match St. Louis City’s 17‑point record for an expansion team. Portland’s record against expansion clubs drops to 6‑7‑1. The Timbers will face New York Red Bulls next, while San Diego hosts Minnesota United.

title: San Diego FC garantiza su lugar en los Playoffs de la MLS 2025
content: San Diego FC, in its inaugural MLS season, secured a playoff berth after a series of recent results that added valuable points to its tally. The club benefited from a 1-1 draw between FC Dallas and LAFC, a 1-3 defeat for Real Salt Lake against Minnesota United, and a 0-0 stalemate with Portland Timbers, which together allowed the San Diego franchise to lock in a postseason spot. The team currently leads the Western Conference and is closely chasing the Supporters' Shield, standing at 53 points while Philadelphia Union holds 54 in the Eastern Conference. Key players highlighted include Anders Dreyer, Hirving 'Chucky' Lozano, and Luca de la Torre. The article emphasizes that the Snapdragon Stadium club’s early playoff qualification demonstrates its ambition to compete for major objectives in MLS 2025.
